transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (VectorAI Head of ML), Rajesh Patel (Platform Eng), Sophie Almeida (CTO)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect) VectorAI is exploring Redwood for model inference behind their product chat and vector search re-ranker. Main asks: low and predictable latency for 95th pct, SDKs that work with LangChain/LlamaIndex, ability to run in our VPC or dedicated pool, and robust observability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we have about 45 minutes on the agenda today, quick intros?
[00:08] Lina: hi lina here, head of ml at VectorAI, basically overseeing model infra and production llm features.
[00:12] Rajesh: rajesh platform eng, I'll own the integration and networking pieces.
[00:16] Sophie: sophie, cto, quick oversight and procurement questions later.
[00:20] Maya: great, i'm maya at redwood, and owen our se is here to do a quick technical walkthrough. owen over to you.
[00:28] Owen: hey all, hi, quick note on flow: i'll cover SDKs, langchain integrations, gateway options and observability hooks then we'll open to q's.
[00:36] Owen: first question for you lina, can you describe your current stack and what you're evaluating — is this a greenfield service or replacing something?
[00:45] Lina: it's partially replacement, we've been using a mix of hosted endpoints from another provider and some self-hosted microservices. main pain is inconsistent 95th percentile latency during spikes and lack of end-to-end tracing into our app.
[00:58] Rajesh: also data residency — some of our customers require EU-only storage and audit logs.
[01:04] Owen: got it, that maps to redwood's offering: hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, or private/vpc on-prem deploys. tradeoffs are isolation and control vs speed of onboarding.
[01:14] Lina: we're particularly interested in langchain and llamain — sorry, llamaindex connectors. how much work is it to swap?
[01:22] Owen: we have first-class SDKs for python and node. and we've got example integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex; most customers just swap the client call to Redwood's client and then use the existing LLM wrapper. i'll share the repo after the call.
[01:33] Owen: small caveats: if you rely on sync streaming vs token-by-token streaming there are some helper adapters, but nothing major.
[01:40] Rajesh: can we see an example of a chain using the retriever + re-ranker pipeline? that's our main flow: vector search -> llm re-ranker -> summarization.
[01:49] Owen: sure, we'll include a sample with retriever pattern. our re-ranker can be hosted model variants or you can route to a cheaper model for scoring — we have routing policies.
[01:58] Sophie: on routing, does redwood support gateway/proxy patterns? can we put a proxy in between for audit/enrichment?
[02:05] Maya: yes you can use an edge gateway or our api gateway; many customers run an internal proxy that authenticates and enriches requests then forwards to redwood. key is ensuring you keep the kv cache prefixing intact if you're doing prefix caching.
[02:17] Rajesh: what's the recommended approach for rate limits and quotas? we have bursty traffic during business hours and want graceful rejection not 429 storms.
[02:25] Owen: we support per-api-key rate limits, per-route quotas, and token-based throttling. we also have smoothing and leaky-bucket policies — and the dedicated offering gives you predictable throughput so you avoid noisy neighbor issues. for hosted we'll recommend quotas and backoff strategies in the client.
[02:39] Lina: curious about observability — do you expose traces and token-level cost breakdowns? we need to tie inference traces to our distributed tracing.
[02:46] Owen: yes, we emit request-level traces and span IDs you can attach to your trace. we also provide token-level cost, latency by token and per-route dashboards in the console. there's a tracing hook header you can pass (x-redwood-trace-id) that appears in our logs.
[02:58] Rajesh: are logs PII redacted? we need to ensure sensitive user content is not stored or is redacted per customer rules.
[03:05] Maya: we support configurable retention and redaction rules. with private deployments you can keep everything on-prem; with hosted you can request contract-level retention and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:16] Sophie: SOC2 and ISO — have you done these? procurement will want to see docs.
[03:20] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II in 2025, ISO in progress. we'll send the security pack and SOC2 report post-call.
[03:27] Lina: performance — do you have numbers for p95 at 1k token responses on A100 or comparable? our profiled generator uses ~700 tokens typically.
[03:36] Owen: numbers vary by model and quantization; for dedicated pools on A100/80gb we see p95 ~ 180-250ms per 256 token chunk for our optimized fp16 path — but again depends on batch size, concurrency. for hosted smaller instances we give profiles in the model catalog; i'll attach the performance spreadsheet.
[03:52] Rajesh: how does batching affect latency? we need consistent sub-300ms p95 for production.
[03:57] Owen: continuous batching helps cost but can hurt single-request latency. we have workload-aware batching: low-latency routes can be pinned to a small batch size and pre-warmed workers in Dedicated. if you need hard SLOs, Dedicated with reserved workers is recommended.
[04:12] Lina: and private deployment options — what's the effort and timeline? we might have to go VPC or on-prem for certain customers.
[04:19] Maya: Private (VPC) option gives a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC, usually a few weeks to provision with infra team alignment. On-prem air-gapped packages take longer and are enterprise engagements. we'll share a checklist for network/firewall rules.
[04:31] Rajesh: about SDK auth patterns — do you support short-lived tokens, mTLS? we're trying to avoid long-lived keys in frontend.
[04:38] Owen: yes, short-lived tokens via our auth service is supported; mTLS is available for private/dedicated. for browser clients we recommend proxying through your backend to avoid exposing secrets.
[04:48] Sophie: curious about model versioning and rollouts, we have frequent model updates and need controlled canary.
[04:54] Maya: rollouts are supported — per-route model pinning, canary percentages, and automatic fallback policies if the canary fails. Console exposes rollout config.
[05:02] Lina: one subtle thing: we use LlamaIndex heavily for retrieval augmented generation, and sometimes the naming of model attributes in connectors breaks. do you have a maintained connector?
[05:11] Owen: we maintain a LangChain integration and a community LlamaIndex connector. sometimes LlamaIndex APIs change; we keep a reference adapter and we'll include a patch list.
[05:19] Rajesh: what's the recommended network topology if we keep a proxy? we'd want low latency to the proxy then to redwood region. can we use private link?
[05:27] Owen: yes private link/direct connect options exist for Dedicated and Private. for hosted standard TLS over internet is common but you can set up a VPC peering or PrivateLink for dedicated lanes.
[05:35] Sophie: any known gotchas when using a gateway that mutates requests? example: adding session metadata to the prompt that changes the token count and affects billing.
[05:44] Owen: good callout — you should account for middleware token amplification. we recommend log sampling and token-count tracing so you can reconcile cost. the token-level reporting helps debug unexpected cost jumps.
[05:56] Lina: on quotas, can we configure soft-limits for staging vs prod? and per-team keys?
[06:03] Maya: yes multi-tenant key support with per-key quotas, env-based policies are supported. staging team keys can be allowed higher error tolerance.
[06:10] Rajesh: demo request: can we run a quick sample request now? maybe a small python snippet to show latency?
[06:15] Owen: we can do a quick curl or python but network to your IP won't reflect dedicated numbers. want me to run a small hosted example to demonstrate SDK streaming?
[06:24] Lina: sure, if it's fast.
[06:27] Owen: (types) sending a small python snippet in chat... "from redwood import Client; c=Client(api_key='REDACTED'); r=c.generate(model='redwood-rlhf-1', prompt='Summarize...')" output.... and shows streaming tokens.
[06:44] Maya: noted — we'll add that snippet to the repo and include a streaming adapter for LangChain.
[06:49] Sophie: procurement note — what's typical contract length for Dedicated? we have budgeting cycles.
[06:54] Maya: typical is annual reserved commitments but month-to-month bursts for scaling; we'll include options in the pricing doc.
[06:59] Rajesh: security again — kms, hsm, and audit logs availability?
[07:03] Owen: we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private, HSM options for enterprise key custody, and audit logs for every request (with retention settings).
[07:12] Lina: if we flow logs into our SIEM will the trace IDs correlate? can we embed span ids in log shipping?
[07:19] Owen: yes you can pass x-redwood-trace-id and we can output logs to your S3/ELK with that field. we'll share the log schema.
[07:28] Maya: ok let's recap next steps...
[07:31] Maya: action items: maya sends pricing and sizing, owen shares langchain/llamaindex repo + code samples, lina shares traffic profile and SLOs, then we schedule a benchmark.
[07:45] Lina: sounds good, one question — latency SLO is 300ms p95, cost target is $0.02 per 1k tokens usable, is that realistic?
[07:55] Owen: cost depends on model and quantization; you can often hit sub-$0.02 with quantized 4-bit models for embeddings/rerankers, but generation at high quality typically costs more. we'll include cost profiles.
[08:09] Rajesh: timeline — we want a POC in q2, ideally pilot in 4 weeks.
[08:15] Maya: feasible — we'll prioritize the benchmark and get you the materials by next week.
[08:20] Sophie: procurement will request SOC2 and contract template — send that.
[08:24] Maya: yes will send security pack.
[08:27] Owen: small technical note — if you need native LlamaIndex callouts we recommend pinning a tokenizer version to keep token counts stable.
[08:35] Lina: noted.
[08:37] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the repo links, pricing, and schedule.
[08:41] Sophie: thanks all.
[08:43] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns like LlamaIndex were transcribed as 'llamain' in a snippet; timestamps approximate.
